clue.text: Band of stars showing class in Sinatra number

indicators.note: the word for class sits inside the song title, so in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: My Way is Frank Sinatra's signature song
ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A group of celebrities performing stylishly in a Sinatra song.
explanation.definitionFit: The galaxy we live in appears from Earth as a pale band of stars across the night sky.

clue.text: Complaint from youth in spring month

indicators.note: the youth is placed within the month, so in signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: May is a month of spring in the northern hemisphere
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A grumble coming from a young person during the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment, which is what a malady is.

clue.text: Desire Liberal associated with marital consent

parts.note: I do is the vow of consent spoken at a wedding

explanation.surface: A wish of a liberal-minded person tied to agreeing to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire or drive, a Freudian term for the urge behind it.

clue.text: Little jumper perhaps in Argyle knit?

indicators.note: to knit is to work yarn into a new form, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A small sweater, maybe, knitted in an Argyle diamond pattern?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater, fitting Argyle knitwear, but here it is a young horse that jumps. The anagram of IN ARGYLE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, and horses are jumpers, so a young one is a little jumper as an example.

clue.text: Alpha male in scrap

parts.note: Alpha is the NATO alphabet word for A
a tom is a male cat, hence a male

explanation.surface: The dominant man getting into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fight, but it is the definition as a tiny fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means a tiny bit, and the smallest particle of matter is a byword for a minute amount.

clue.text: Mamma Mia finally shown in French port

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the name of the port, so in signals insertion here

parts.note: Brest is a naval port in Brittany, France

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Mia

explanation.surface: The musical Mamma Mia at last being staged in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mamma Mia' reads as the ABBA musical, but Mamma alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamma is the anatomical term for the milk-producing gland, the human bosom.

clue.text: Rugby forward finds bear in Nutwood

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
forward in the sense of cheeky or impudent means pert

explanation.surface: A rugby forward comes across a bear in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby forward' wants to be one position on the field; it splits into RU and a synonym of cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character who lives in the village of Nutwood.

clue.text: Amusing tale one acted out

indicators.note: acted out suggests the words are performed in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A funny story that someone performed on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining story about a real incident.

clue.text: Aroused? By implication no!

parts.note: the clue word no, when turned round, gives the letters on, so the wordplay describes how it was made

explanation.surface: An exclamation of denial at being called aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: turn the letters of ON round and you get NO, the word the clue prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excited or stimulated, especially sexually, is the phrasal-verb sense of switched on in that way.

clue.text: Arab lord at sea finds Canadian peninsula

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An Arab nobleman sailing discovers a peninsula in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The large peninsula in eastern Canada, between Hudson Bay and the Atlantic, bears this name.

clue.text: Ace paper after correction to be published

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: a corrected text has its errors fixed, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excellent newspaper, once edited, is ready to go to print.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or article is said to come out in print when it is issued, a standard publishing sense.

clue.text: Outgoing writers plunged into Devon river

indicators.note: the writers are dropped inside the river, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England, flowing through Exeter
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: Sociable authors take a dip in a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outgoing' looks like an adjective for friendly, but it is a noun: money going out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, as a noun, is money spent, which is a cost or outlay.

clue.text: Benefit sheltering theologian in breeze

indicators.note: the benefit word shelters the theologian inside it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A welfare payment protecting a religious scholar out in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breeze' reads as wind, but it means something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is informal for an easy task, and a doddle is British slang for the same.

clue.text: Where animal comes across university pair?

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
a bridge is the structure by which one crosses over

explanation.surface: A spot where cattle cross a river, as a riddle about two universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The blend of Oxford and Cambridge names England's two oldest universities as a pair.

clue.text: Cobblers fitting sole in alcove

indicators.note: the sole word is placed within the alcove word, so in signals insertion

parts.note: a bay is a recess or alcove in a wall
sole means only or lone

explanation.surface: Shoe repairers attaching a sole in a recess of their shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' reads as shoemakers, matching 'sole', but it is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers is British slang for rubbish talk, which baloney also means in American usage.

clue.text: Footwear for one moving surreptitiously?

definitions.meaning: a soft rubber-soled shoe, a trainer

explanation.surface: Soft shoes suited to someone creeping around quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft-soled shoe is the American name for a trainer, and literally someone who sneaks.

clue.text: German managed to escape Otranto

indicators.note: the managed word escapes, getting out of the place name, so it is removed

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: A German succeeded in getting away from the Italian town of Otranto.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a typical German man's given name, so it stands for a German as an example.

clue.text: One wandering sailor in van with dog barking

indicators.note: the sailor is placed within the scrambled letters, so in signals insertion
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman living in a van with a noisy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise but is British slang for mad, signalling the anagram that gives VAGOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a homeless wanderer who moves from place to place.

clue.text: Nothing stops faulty crumpet processor

indicators.note: nothing plugs a gap in the jumbled letters, as a stopper fills a hole
a faulty item is broken, so the letters of the bread are rearranged

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing halts a defective crumpet machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' turns CRUMPET into CMPUTER, and O stops the gap after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A data processor is a machine that processes information electronically.

clue.text: Two insects circling husband, someone huge

indicators.note: the insects circle around the husband, so they contain him

parts.note: a bee and a moth are two insects

explanation.surface: A pair of bugs buzzing around a married man, who is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge creature from the Bible, used of anything enormous.

clue.text: Bath water in which Virginia rotated leg

indicators.note: rotated means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia turns her leg in the bathwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath water' reads as a tub, but it is the English city of Bath, through which this river flows. In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The river through the city of Bath in England is its water in the sense of a watercourse.

clue.text: Roll stuffed with old chicken

indicators.note: the roll is filled with the old letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster

explanation.surface: A bread roll filled with leftover chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' reads as bread to suit the filling, but it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is the male of the domestic chicken species.

clue.text: Detective leaving North American land once?

indicators.note: the detective leaves, departing from the word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a Canadian is a North American
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective departing from a North American country long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Promised Land was the ancient region roughly of modern Israel and Palestine.

clue.text: Short old French person grabbing tea cake

indicators.note: the shortened word grabs and holds the drink inside it
short means cut off at the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a Gaul was an inhabitant of ancient Gaul, the old France

explanation.surface: A small Frenchman of old snatching tea and cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes the last letter of GAUL to give GAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Olympic medal for Brown

definitions.meaning: the medal awarded for third place
a reddish-brown metallic colour, as a verb to tan

explanation.surface: An Olympic prize awarded to someone named Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The third-place prize is of this metal, and its colour is a yellowish brown, also to tan.

clue.text: Character set to move a table outside pub

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go outside the pub abbreviation, enclosing it
to move the letters is to put them in a new order

parts.note: PH is short for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: A group of people prepares to shift a table out of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' turns A TABLE into ALABET, which goes around PH.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters used to write a language is a set of characters.

clue.text: Live, then hide in Los Angeles region

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a lair is a hiding place for an animal

explanation.surface: Settle down and then go into hiding in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel Air is a wealthy residential neighbourhood on the west side of Los Angeles.

clue.text: Monied Manhattan street with everything?

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A rich New York avenue that has it all?
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street, in lower Manhattan, is New York's financial district and byword for money.

clue.text: Fugitive away from home turf endlessly

parts.note: out means not at home

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lawn is an area of turf

explanation.surface: A runaway kept off home ground for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the last letter of LAWN to give LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a criminal on the run from justice, a fugitive.

clue.text: Refusal abroad to accept a European emperor

indicators.note: the refusal accepts, taking in, the other pieces inside it

parts.note: non is French for no
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A foreign rejection of a European ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: American lawyer to call for courage

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecutor
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A US attorney needs to summon up bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring as a noun is boldness or bravery, a synonym of courage.

clue.text: Boozer — he turned into a swine!

indicators.note: the turned letters go into the swine phrase, inside it

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a swine

indicators.note: turned means the word he is read backwards

explanation.surface: A drunk is transformed into a pig, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' reads as a drinker, but it is British slang for a pub. 'turned' makes EH from HE, going into A LOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a pub, a place where beer is served.
